claim: HIV has been reported to be cytotoxic in vitro and in lymph node infection models.
source: HIV has been reported to be cytotoxic in vitro and in lymph node infection models.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript to prior work.

claim: Partial inhibition of transmissions of multiple virions per cell could lead to increased numbers of live infected cells.
source: Using a computational approach, we found that partial inhibition of transmissions of multiple virions per cell could lead to increased numbers of live infected cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational model described in the manuscript.

claim: If the number of viral DNA copies remains above one after inhibition, then eliminating the surplus viral copies reduces cell death.
source: If the number of viral DNA copies remains above one after inhibition, then eliminating the surplus viral copies reduces cell death.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational model and experimental observations.

claim: Increased numbers of live infected cells were observed when infection was partially inhibited with the antiretroviral efavirenz in a cell line.
source: Using a cell line, we observed increased numbers of live infected cells when infection was partially inhibited with the antiretroviral efavirenz or neutralizing antibody.
evidence: This is an experimental finding reported in the abstract and detailed in the Results section.

claim: Increased numbers of live infected cells were observed when infection was partially inhibited with neutralizing antibody in a cell line.
source: Using a cell line, we observed increased numbers of live infected cells when infection was partially inhibited with the antiretroviral efavirenz or neutralizing antibody.
evidence: This is an experimental finding reported in the abstract and detailed in the Results section.

claim: More live infected lymph node cells were observed when lymph node infection by partially resistant HIV mutants was inhibited with efavirenz at concentrations reported in lymph nodes.
source: We then used efavirenz at concentrations reported in lymph nodes to inhibit lymph node infection by partially resistant HIV mutants. We observed more live infected lymph node cells, but with fewer HIV DNA copies per cell, relative to no drug.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection experiments.

claim: Lymph node cells infected with partially resistant HIV mutants and treated with efavirenz had fewer HIV DNA copies per cell relative to no drug.
source: We observed more live infected lymph node cells, but with fewer HIV DNA copies per cell, relative to no drug.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection experiments.

claim: Limited attenuation of HIV transmission per cell may increase live infected cell numbers in environments where the force of infection is high.
source: Hence, counterintuitively, limited attenuation of HIV transmission per cell may increase live infected cell numbers in environments where the force of infection is high.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and computational findings.

claim: HIV infection results in extensive T cell depletion in lymph node environments.
source: HIV infection is known to result in extensive T cell depletion in lymph node environments (Sanchez et al., 2015), where infection is most robust (Brenchley et al., 2004; Doitsh et al., 2010; Doitsh et al., 2014; Finkel et al., 1995; Galloway et al., 2015; Mattapallil et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Infection is most robust in lymph node environments.
source: HIV infection is known to result in extensive T cell depletion in lymph node environments (Sanchez et al., 2015), where infection is most robust (Brenchley et al., 2004; Doitsh et al., 2010; Doitsh et al., 2014; Finkel et al., 1995; Galloway et al., 2015; Mattapallil et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Depletion of HIV infectable target cells, in addition to onset of immune control, is thought to account for the decreased replication ratio of HIV from an initial peak in early infection.
source: Depletion of HIV infectable target cells, in addition to onset of immune control, is thought to account for the decreased replication ratio of HIV from an initial peak in early infection (Bonhoeffer et al., 1997; Nowak and May, 2000; Perelson, 2002; Phillips, 1996; Quiñones-Mateu and Arts, 2006; Ribeiro et al., 2010; Wodarz and Levy, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Individuals are most infectious in the initial, acute stage of infection, where the target cell population is relatively intact and produces high viral loads.
source: This is consistent with observations that individuals are most infectious in the initial, acute stage of infection, where the target cell population is relatively intact and produces high viral loads (Hollingsworth et al., 2008; Wawer et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: T-cell death occurs by several mechanisms, which are either directly or indirectly mediated by HIV infection.
source: T-cell death occurs by several mechanisms, which are either directly or indirectly mediated by HIV infection.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by the subsequent detailed mechanisms described in the text.

claim: Accumulation of incompletely reverse transcribed HIV transcripts is sensed by interferon-γ–inducible protein 16.
source: Accumulation of incompletely reverse transcribed HIV transcripts is sensed by interferon-γ–inducible protein 16 (Monroe et al., 2014) and leads to pyroptotic death of incompletely infected cells by initiating a cellular defence program involving the activation of caspase 1 (Doitsh et al., 2010; Doitsh et al., 2014; Galloway et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Accumulation of incompletely reverse transcribed HIV transcripts leads to pyroptotic death of incompletely infected cells by initiating a cellular defence program involving the activation of caspase 1.
source: Accumulation of incompletely reverse transcribed HIV transcripts is sensed by interferon-γ–inducible protein 16 (Monroe et al., 2014) and leads to pyroptotic death of incompletely infected cells by initiating a cellular defence program involving the activation of caspase 1 (Doitsh et al., 2010; Doitsh et al., 2014; Galloway et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: HIV proteins Tat and Env have been shown to lead to cell death of infected cells through CD95-mediated apoptosis following T-cell activation.
source: HIV proteins Tat and Env have also been shown to lead to cell death of infected cells through CD95-mediated apoptosis following T-cell activation (Banda et al., 1992; Westendorp et al., 1995a; Westendorp et al., 1995b1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Damage to lymph nodes due to chronic immune activation leads to an environment less conducive to T-cell survival.
source: Using SIV infection, it has been shown that damage to lymph nodes due to chronic immune activation leads to an environment less conducive to T-cell survival (Zeng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research using SIV infection.

claim: Double strand breaks in the host DNA caused by integration of the reverse transcribed virus results in cell death by the DNA-PK-mediated activation of the p53 response.
source: Finally, double strand breaks in the host DNA caused by integration of the reverse transcribed virus results in cell death by the DNA-PK-mediated activation of the p53 response (Cooper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The lymph node environment is conducive to HIV infection due to presence of infectable cells.
source: The lymph node environment is conducive to HIV infection due to: (1) presence of infectable cells (Deleage et al., 2016; Embretson et al., 1993; Tenner-Racz et al., 1998);
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The lymph node environment is conducive to HIV infection due to proximity of cells to each other and lack of flow which should enable cell-to-cell HIV spread.
source: (2) proximity of cells to each other and lack of flow which should enable cell-to-cell HIV spread (Baxter et al., 2014; Dale et al., 2011; Groot et al., 2008; Groppelli et al., 2015; Gummuluru et al., 2002; Hübner et al., 2009; Jolly et al., 2004; Jolly et al., 2011; Münch et al., 2007; Sherer et al., 2007; Sourisseau et al., 2007; Sowinski et al., 2008);
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The lymph node environment is conducive to HIV infection due to decreased penetration of antiretroviral therapy.
source: (3) decreased penetration of antiretroviral therapy (ART) (Fletcher et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Multiple infections per cell have been reported in cell-to-cell spread of HIV.
source: Multiple infections per cell have been reported in cell-to-cell spread of HIV (Baxter et al., 2014; Boullé et al., 2016; Dang et al., 2004; Del Portillo et al., 2011; Dixit and Perelson, 2004; Duncan et al., 2013; Law et al., 2016; Reh et al., 2015; Russell et al., 2013; Sigal et al., 2011; Zhong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In cell-to-cell mode of HIV transmission, an interaction between the infected donor cell and the uninfected target results in directed transmission of large numbers of virions.
source: In this mode of HIV transmission, an interaction between the infected donor cell and the uninfected target results in directed transmission of large numbers of virions (Baxter et al., 2014; Groppelli et al., 2015; Hübner et al., 2009; Sowinski et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cell-to-cell route is thought to be the main cause of multiple infections per cell.
source: However, the cell-to-cell route is thought to be the main cause of multiple infections per cell (Hübner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Several studies showed multiple infections in the lymph nodes.
source: In the lymph nodes, several studies showed multiple infections (Gratton et al., 2000; Jung et al., 2002; Law et al., 2016) while another study did not (Josefsson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: One study did not show multiple infections in the lymph nodes.
source: In the lymph nodes, several studies showed multiple infections (Gratton et al., 2000; Jung et al., 2002; Law et al., 2016) while another study did not (Josefsson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: T cells were shown not to be multiply infected in the peripheral blood compartment.
source: For example, T cells were shown not to be multiply infected in the peripheral blood compartment (Josefsson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The average number of HIV DNA copies per cell is greater than one in 3 out of 12 individuals in the CD3-positive, CD32a high CD4 T-cell subset in the face of ART.
source: However, more recent work investigating markers associated with HIV latency in the face of ART found that the average number of HIV DNA copies per cell is greater than one in 3 out of 12 individuals. This occurred in the face of ART in the CD3-positive, CD32a high CD4 T-cell subset (Descours et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Multiple viral integration attempts per cell may increase the probability of death.
source: Multiple viral integration attempts per cell may increase the probability of death.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction and tested in the manuscript.

claim: Attenuation of infection may increase viral replication by increasing the number of live targets.
source: One consequence of HIV-mediated death may be that attenuation of infection may increase viral replication by increasing the number of live targets.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: It has been suggested that more attenuated HIV strains result in more successful infections in terms of the ability of the virus to replicate in the infected individual.
source: Indeed, it has been suggested that more attenuated HIV strains result in more successful infections in terms of the ability of the virus to replicate in the infected individual (Ariën et al., 2005; Nowak and May, 2000; Payne et al., 2014; Quiñones-Mateu and Arts, 2006; Wodarz and Levy, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Partially inhibiting infection with drug or antibody resulted in an increase in the number of live infected cells in both a cell line and in lymph node cells.
source: We observed that partially inhibiting infection with drug or antibody resulted in an increase in the number of live infected cells in both a cell line and in lymph node cells.
evidence: This is an experimental finding reported in the Results section.

claim: This is the first experimental demonstration at the cellular level that attenuation of HIV infection can result in an increase in live infected cells under specific infection conditions.
source: This is, to our knowledge, the first experimental demonstration at the cellular level that attenuation of HIV infection can result in an increase in live infected cells under specific infection conditions.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: The probability of successful infection of a target cell given n infection attempts is 1-(1-r)^n.
source: The probability of successful infection of a target cell given n infection attempts is 1-(1 r)n (Sigal et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a mathematical model equation supported by a citation.

claim: The probability of a cell to survive infection in the face of n infection attempts is Ln=(1-q)^n.
source: We define Ln as the probability of a cell to survive infection in the face of n infection attempts. Assuming infection attempts act independently, Ln=(1-q)n.
evidence: This is a mathematical model definition.

claim: At each drug strength d/λ, Pλ increases as the probability of infection r increases.
source: Analysis of the probability of a cell to survive and be infected as a function of r and q shows that at each drug strength d/λ, Pλ increases as the probability of infection r increases (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the mathematical model analysis, supported by Figure 1.

claim: A subset of parameter values results in a peak in the number of infected cells at intermediate d/λ, decreasing as drug strength increases further.
source: A subset of parameter values results in a peak in the number of infected cells at intermediate d/λ, decreasing as drug strength increases further (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the mathematical model analysis, supported by Figure 1.

claim: As q increases, the cost of multiple infections per cell increases, and the infection optimum shifts to higher d/λ values.
source: As q increases, the cost of multiple infections per cell increases, and the infection optimum shifts to higher d/λ values.
evidence: This is a finding from the mathematical model analysis.

claim: A fall from the infection optimum at decreasing d/λ is driven by increasing cell death as a result of increasing infection attempts per cell.
source: A fall from the infection optimum at decreasing d/λ is driven by increasing cell death as a result of increasing infection attempts per cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mathematical model results.

claim: About one quarter of ACH-2 cells showed a PCR product of the expected size when assayed for HIV DNA.
source: We sorted a total of 166 ACH-2 cells at one cell per well into lysis buffer and subdivided single-cell lysates into four wells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A). About one quarter of cells showed a PCR product of the expected size.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ACH-2 cell analysis.

claim: Cells with more than one HIV copy per cell in ACH-2 cells were very rare and may reflect either errors in cell sorting or dividing cells.
source: Cells with more than one HIV copy per cell were very rare and may reflect either errors in cell sorting or dividing cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with a speculative interpretation.

claim: The frequency of detection in ACH-2 cells indicated the detection efficiency per HIV DNA copy.
source: Given that each ACH-2 cell contains one HIV DNA copy, the frequency of detection indicated our detection efficiency per HIV DNA copy.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ACH-2 experimental results.

claim: In coculture infection with approximately 2% infected donor cells, 60 GFP-positive cells were assayed and obtained a wide distribution of viral DNA copies per cell, which ranged from 0 to 9 copies.
source: We used approximately 2% infected donor cells as our input, and detected the number of HIV DNA copies per cell by flow cytometric sorting of individual GFP-positive cells followed by splitting each cell lysate over 10 wells. Wells were then amplified by PCR and visualized on an agarose gel (Figure 2A). We assayed 60 cells and obtained a wide distribution of viral DNA copies per cell, which ranged from 0 to 9 copies (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from coculture infection.

claim: In cell-free HIV infection, either zero or one HIV copy per cell was detected in 30 GFP-positive cells.
source: We also detected the HIV copy number in 30 GFP-positive cells infected by cell-free HIV. HIV in cell-free form was obtained by filtering supernatant from HIV producing cells to exclude cells or cell fragments, then infecting target cells with the filtered virus. Infection with this virus is defined here as cell-free infection. In this case, we detected either zero or one HIV copy per cell (Figure 2B inset).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell-free infection.

claim: The frequency of single HIV DNA copies in cell-free infection was 0.23, identical to the measured result in the ACH-2 cell line.
source: The frequency of single HIV DNA copies was 0.23, identical to the measured result in the ACH-2 cell line.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental results.

claim: On average, 15 ± 3 copies per cell were obtained after correction for detection sensitivity in coculture infection.
source: We computationally corrected the detected number of DNA copies in coculture infection for the sensitivity of our PCR reaction as determined by the ACH-2 results (Materials and methods). On average we obtained 15 ± 3 copies per cell after correction.
evidence: This is an experimental finding after computational correction.

claim: Cell-free infection with EFV showed a monotonic decrease with IC50 = 2.9 nM and Hill coefficient of 2.1.
source: Fit of the model to the cell-free data using wild type, EFV-sensitive HIV showed a monotonic decrease with IC50 = 2.9 nM and Hill coefficient of 2.1 (Figure 2C, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to a model.

claim: A peak in the number of live infected target cells was observed at 4 nM EFV in coculture infection.
source: We observed a peak in the number of live infected target cells at 4 nM EFV (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from coculture infection with EFV.

claim: Equation (3) best fit the behaviour of infection when r = 0.22 and q = 0.17, resulting in a peak at 4.8 nM EFV.
source: Equation (3) best fit the behaviour of infection when r = 0.22 and q = 0.17, resulting in a peak at 4.8 nM EFV (Figure 2D, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to the mathematical model.

claim: An infection optimum is present in the cell line infection system.
source: Hence an infection optimum is present in the cell line infection system.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Measured r and q values were 0.28 ± 0.08 and 0.15 ± 0.07 (mean ±standard deviation), respectively.
source: Measured r and q values were 0.28 ± 0.08 and 0.15 ± 0.07 (mean ±standard deviation), respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental measurement of model parameters.

claim: The solution to Equation (3) using measured r and q values showed similar behavior to the solution with the fitted values for wild-type HIV infection.
source: The solution to Equation (3) using these values showed similar behavior to the solution with the fitted values for wild-type HIV infection, indicating that the fitted values gave a reasonable approximation of the behavior of the system (Figure 2D, dashed green line).
evidence: This is a comparison of model predictions with different parameter values.

claim: Time-lapse microscopy showed deterioration in the number of live cells in the time-lapse culture starting at 1 day post-infection when no drug was added.
source: In order to investigate the dynamics of cell depletion due to cell-to-cell HIV spread and its modulation by the addition of an inhibitor, we performed time-lapse microscopy over a two day infection window. While infection parameters were different due to the constraints of visualizing cells (Materials and methods), the general trend from the data was deterioration in the number of live cells in the time-lapse culture starting at 1 day post-infection when no drug was added.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from time-lapse microscopy.

claim: The deterioration in live cell numbers was averted by the addition of EFV in time-lapse microscopy experiments.
source: The deterioration in live cell numbers was averted by the addition of EFV (Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from time-lapse microscopy.

claim: The L100I mutant was obtained by culturing wild-type HIV in the reporter cell line in the presence of EFV.
source: We next investigated whether an infection optimum occurs with EFV-resistant HIV. To derive the resistant mutant, we cultured wild-type HIV in our reporter cell line in the presence of EFV. We obtained the L100I partially resistant mutant.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method to generate the mutant.

claim: The L100I mutant was found to have an IC50 = 29 nM EFV and a Hill coefficient of 2.0.
source: The L100I mutant was found to have an IC50 = 29 nM EFV and a Hill coefficient of 2.0 (Figure 3A, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to a model.

claim: There was a peak in the number of live infected target cells for the L100I mutant infection at 40 nM EFV.
source: Similarly to wild-type HIV coculture infection, there was a peak in the number of live infected target cells for the L100I mutant infection. However, the peak in live infected cells was shifted to 40 nM EFV (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from coculture infection with the L100I mutant.

claim: Fits to Equation (3) for L100I mutant infection recapitulated the experimental results when r = 0.29 and q = 0.13, with a fitted peak at 45 nM EFV.
source: Fits were obtained to Equation (3) using dmut values and λ measured for wild-type infection. The fits recapitulated the experimental results when r = 0.29 and q = 0.13, with a fitted peak at 45 nM EFV (Figure 3B, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to the mathematical model.

claim: A peak in live infected cells was obtained at 5 ug/ml b12 antibody.
source: In order to examine whether a peak in live infected targets can be obtained with an unrelated inhibitor, we used the HIV neutralizing antibody b12. This antibody is effective against cell-to-cell spread of HIV (Baxter et al., 2014; Reh et al., 2015). We obtained a peak in live infected cells at 5 ug/ml b12 (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an experimental finding using b12 antibody.

claim: The b12 concentration that resulted in a peak number of live infected cells was the same for wild-type virus and the L100I mutant.
source: The b12 concentration that resulted in a peak number of live infected cells was the same for wild-type virus and the L100I mutant, showing that L100I mutant fitness gain was EFV specific.
evidence: This is an experimental finding comparing wild-type and mutant responses to b12.

claim: Cell-free infection in the face of b12 showed a sharp and monotonic drop in live infected cells for both wild type and mutant virus.
source: In contrast, cell-free infection in the face of b12 showed a sharp and monotonic drop in live infected cells for both wild type and mutant virus (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell-free infection with b12.

claim: In each of the lymph nodes tested, a peak in live infected cells was observed at intermediate EFV concentrations.
source: In each of the lymph nodes tested, we observed a peak in live infected cells at intermediate EFV concentrations.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection experiments.

claim: Lymph node cells from participant 205 showed a peak of live infected cells at 100 nM EFV.
source: Lymph node cells from participant 205 showed a peak of live infected cells at 100 nM EFV (Figure 5A, first row).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection.

claim: The infection optimum in the lymph node cells of study participant 257 was visible as a plateau between 50 and 200 nM EFV.
source: The infection optimum in the lymph node cells of study participant 257 was visible as a plateau between 50 and 200 nM EFV.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection.

claim: In the presence of EFV, there was a decrease in the fraction of dead cells that was offset by a similar increase in the fraction of live infected cells for lymph nodes from all participants.
source: In the presence of EFV, there was a decrease in the fraction of dead cells that was offset by a similar increase in the fraction of live infected cells for lymph nodes from all participants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from lymph node infection experiments.

claim: Cells from lymph node participant 251 showed an infection optimum at 50 nM EFV.
source: Cells from this lymph node showed an infection optimum at 50 nM EFV (Figure 5A, third row).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection.

claim: Multiple DNA copies were observed in EFV-untreated lymph node cells, and the number of copies decreased with EFV.
source: We observed multiple DNA copies in EFV-untreated lymph node cells. The number of copies decreased with EFV (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection.

claim: The corrected numbers of HIV DNA copies were 21 with no drug, and five copies in the presence of EFV at the infection optimum in lymph node cells.
source: The corrected numbers were 21 HIV DNA copies with no drug, and five copies in the presence of EFV at the infection optimum (Figure 5C, see Figure 5—figure supplement 2 for histograms of raw HIV DNA copy numbers per cell).
evidence: This is an experimental finding after correction for detection sensitivity.

claim: The K103N mutant showed a monotonic decrease with IC50 = 26.0 nM and Hill coefficient of 1.5 in cell-free infection.
source: The fits showed a monotonic decrease with IC50 = 26.0 nM and Hill coefficient of 1.5 (Figure 6A, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to a model.

claim: An infection optimum with EFV was observed in lymph node cells infected with the K103N mutant, with the peak in the number of live infected cells between 80 and 160 nM EFV.
source: We observed an infection optimum with EFV in lymph node cells. The peak in the number of live infected cells in the presence of drug was between 80 and 160 nM EFV (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from lymph node infection with K103N mutant.

claim: Fits to Equation (3) for K103N mutant infection recapitulated the experimental results when r = 0.91 and q = 0.15, with a fitted peak at 90 nM EFV.
source: The fits recapitulated the experimental results when r = 0.91 and q = 0.15, with a fitted peak at 90 nM EFV (Figure 6B, black line).
evidence: This is a result from fitting experimental data to the mathematical model.

claim: No clear dependence on EFV in the absence of infection was detected in lymph node cells.
source: To examine if the observed peak in live cells may be due to EFV alone, we measured cell viability in lymph node cells from one of the study participants used in the above experiment as a function of EFV without infection. No clear dependence on EFV in the absence of infection was detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an experimental control to rule out EFV toxicity as the cause of the observed peak.

claim: The optimal virulence concept in ecology proposes that virulence needs to be balanced against host survival for optimal pathogen spread.
source: The optimal virulence concept in ecology proposes that virulence needs to be balanced against host survival for optimal pathogen spread (Bonhoeffer et al., 1996; Bonhoeffer and Nowak, 1994; Gandon et al., 2001; Jensen et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a concept from ecology supported by citations.

claim: At the cellular level, optimal virulence implies that the number of successfully infected cells may increase when infection virulence is reduced.
source: At the cellular level, this implies that the number of successfully infected cells may increase when infection virulence is reduced.
evidence: This is an inference from the optimal virulence concept applied to cellular infection.

claim: In the case where cells were infected by single infection attempts, inhibition always led to a decline in the number of live infected cells.
source: Using a model where cells are infected and die in a probabilistic way, we found that there were two possible outcomes of partially inhibiting infection. In the case where cells were infected by single infection attempts, inhibition always led to a decline in the number of live infected cells, since inhibition reduced the number of infections per cell from one to zero.
evidence: This is a finding from the mathematical model.

claim: In the case of multiple infection attempts per cell, the possibility existed that inhibition reduced the number of integrating HIV DNA copies, without extinguishing infection of the cell completely.
source: In contrast, in the case of multiple infection attempts per cell, the possibility existed that inhibition reduced the number of integrating HIV DNA copies, without extinguishing infection of the cell completely.
evidence: This is a finding from the mathematical model.

claim: If each HIV DNA copy increases the probability of cell death, reducing the number of HIV DNA copies without eliminating infection should lead to an increased probability of infected cell survival.
source: If each HIV DNA copy increases the probability of cell death, reducing the number of HIV DNA copies without eliminating infection should lead to an increased probability of infected cell survival.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the model assumptions.

claim: The model as described by Equation (3) reproduced the essential behaviour of the experimental results.
source: Our model as described by Equation (3) reproduced the essential behaviour of the experimental results.
evidence: This is a statement about the model's ability to fit experimental data.

claim: An equivalent model can be constructed assuming a dependence of cell death on infection.
source: However, as shown in the Appendix 1, an equivalent model can be constructed assuming a dependence of cell death on infection.
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative mathematical model formulation.

claim: Neither model accurately captures infection dynamics at high-drug concentrations, away from the infection optimum.
source: Neither model accurately captures infection dynamics at high-drug concentrations, away from the infection optimum.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the models.

claim: An infection optimum in the face of an antiretroviral drug may be important in HIV infection of lymph node cells and may be less pronounced in cells from peripheral blood.
source: Physiologically, an infection optimum in the face of an antiretroviral drug may be important in HIV infection of lymph node cells and may be less pronounced in cells from peripheral blood.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing lymph node and PBMC infection results.

claim: The infection optimum should occur with other classes of antiretroviral drugs, since all drugs should decrease the multiplicity of infection between cells.
source: However, the infection optimum we describe should occur with other classes of antiretroviral drugs, since all drugs should decrease the multiplicity of infection between cells.
evidence: This is a generalization of the findings to other drug classes.

claim: The more complex outcome of partial inhibition of infection should also be considered in other infections where multiple pathogens infect one cell and host cell death is a possible outcome.
source: The more complex outcome of partial inhibition of infection should also be considered in other infections where multiple pathogens infect one cell and host cell death is a possible outcome (Mahamed et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a generalization of the findings to other infections, supported by a citation.

claim: These observations reinforce previous results showing that successful completion of reverse transcription leads to cellular cytotoxicity.
source: These observations reinforce previous results showing that successful completion of reverse transcription leads to cellular cytotoxicity.
evidence: This is a conclusion that connects the current findings to prior research.

claim: The experiments presented reflect the effect of partial inhibition on productive infection of HIV target cells, which mostly consist of activated T-cell subsets, not resting T cells.
source: The experiments presented here reflect the effect of partial inhibition on productive infection of HIV target cells, which mostly consist of activated T-cell subsets, not resting T cells.
evidence: This is a clarification about the cell types studied in the experiments.

claim: This study may have implications for the establishment of viral reservoirs in the context of poorly controlled infections, infections with some degree of drug resistance, or infections where some replication may take place in the face of ART.
source: This study may have implications for the establishment of viral reservoirs in the context of poorly controlled infections, infections with some degree of drug resistance, or infections where some replication may take place in the face of ART, since infected cell survival is a pre-requisite for long-term persistence.
evidence: This is a speculation about the clinical implications of the findings.

claim: The clinical implications of an infection optimum in the presence of EFV with EFV-sensitive HIV strains are likely to be negligible, since the drug concentrations at which the infection optimum occurs are extremely low.
source: The clinical implications of an infection optimum in the presence of EFV with EFV-sensitive HIV strains are likely to be negligible, since the drug concentrations at which the infection optimum occurs are extremely low.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clinical significance of the findings for EFV-sensitive HIV.

claim: For EFV-resistant HIV, the infection optimum shifts to the range of EFV concentrations observed in lymph nodes (~100 nM).
source: However, for EFV-resistant HIV, the infection optimum shifts to the range of EFV concentrations observed in lymph nodes (~100 nM) (Fletcher et al., 2014b), and can be expected to shift to even higher EFV concentrations with more resistant mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental findings with resistant mutants, supported by a citation about EFV concentrations in lymph nodes.

claim: EFV has a longer half-life than the other antiretroviral drugs co-formulated with it.
source: As EFV has a longer half-life than the other antiretroviral drugs co-formulated with it, it may be the only agent present in partially adherent individuals for substantial periods of time (Taylor et al., 2007).

claim: Partial inhibition of HIV infection with EFV may provide a surprising advantage to EFV resistant mutants.

claim: ACH-2 cells contain a single inactive HIV integration per genome.
source: We first measured the number of viral DNA copies in ACH-2 cells, reported to contain a single inactive HIV integration per genome (Chun et al., 1997; O'Doherty et al., 2002).

claim: The L100I mutant does not often occur in the absence of other drug resistance mutations according to the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database.
source: Since L100I does not often occur in the absence of other drug resistance mutations according to the Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database (Rhee et al., 2003), we repeated the experiment with the K103N mutant, a frequently observed mutation in virologic failure with a higher level of resistance to EFV relative to the L100I mutant.
evidence: This is information from a database supported by a citation.
